chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, who said:

Indeed, ʿAbbād al-Makkī said: Sufyān al-Thawrī said to me, "I see that you hold a position with Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, so ask him about a man who committed adultery while he is ill; if the hadd is carried out upon him, they fear that he may die. What do you say about him?" He said: So I asked him, and he said to me, "Is this issue from your own mind, or did someone instruct you to ask about it?" So I said to him, "Sufyān al-Thawrī instructed me to ask you about it."

He said, "Indeed, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was brought a man afflicted with abdominal swelling, whose belly had become bloated and the veins of whose thighs had become visible, and he had committed adultery with a sick woman. So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله commanded, and a palm branch containing one hundred stalks was brought. He struck him with it once and struck her with it once, then let both of them go free. And that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:"
"And take in your hand a bundle, then strike with it, and do not break your oath."

key_terms.ضِغْثاً: a bundle of thin twigs or stalks
key_terms.مِائَةُ شِمْرَاخٍ: one hundred thin stalks or strands

ai.seo_question: How is the hadd for zina applied if the offender is too sick to endure the usual punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the hadd for zina when the offenders are physically ill and there is fear that full corporal punishment would cause death. Imam Abu ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام cites a precedent from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and links it to the Qur'anic wording about striking with a bundle, showing a mitigated mode of carrying out the punishment in such a case.
